definition: A submarine whose presence has been successfully established and which is therefore handled openly by detection-dependent procedures.
A submarine that has not yet been successfully detected and is handled under concealed-information movement procedures.
Detection performed with radar rather than visual or acoustic sensing.
Detection performed with sonar or other acoustic sensing against underwater contacts.
Detection performed by direct observation rather than an electronic or acoustic sensor.
A rating representing a platform's ability to engage hostile aircraft at air-defence ranges.
A rating representing close-in defensive fire against aircraft or incoming threats.
A rating representing an aircraft's ability to attack other aircraft within a particular engagement band.
The closest air-to-air engagement band, associated with dogfighting and short-ranged weapons.
An intermediate air-to-air engagement band between dogfight and long-range combat.
The outer air-to-air engagement band used by aircraft with sufficiently long-ranged weapons.
Fighters assigned to patrol defensively and react to hostile aircraft or detected submarine threats.
A modifier representing how difficult an aircraft is to destroy in air-defence or air-to-air combat.
An aircraft that protects a raid or nearby friendly aircraft by degrading hostile long- or area-range attacks.
An action in which an aircraft discards carried attack stores to remove restrictions associated with a loaded strike configuration.
The position an aircraft must reach before releasing a missile or other stand-off weapon.
The minimum forward distance or interval required between successive heading changes by an aircraft.
The highest altitude level or band an aircraft may occupy.
A test for accidental loss when an aircraft operates in especially hazardous flight conditions.
A combat result that forces an aircraft to disengage or return home without necessarily destroying it.
An aircraft used primarily to search for naval contacts with visual, radar, electronic-support or sonar sensors.
Passive electronic sensing used to detect or locate hostile electromagnetic emitters such as radars.
A measure or category representing how strongly a target reflects radar energy.
A radar's technical upper detection limit imposed by its pulse timing rather than target visibility alone.
Electronic defensive measures that reduce the effectiveness of hostile sensors, missiles or long-range attacks.
A communications link that shares sensor, targeting or tactical information between platforms.
An anti-submarine sensor that searches by means other than conventional acoustic sonar.
An unmanned surface, subsurface or aerial platform represented as a controllable sensor, weapon or support asset.
